answer: An agent marketplace grants each identity one active job slot only after it locks a $100 bond for 90 days. Whether agents plan a voyage, model glacier melt, or price sable fur, the same rule applies. Creating 1,000 fake identities therefore ties up $100,000: new names do not create free capacity. The lock prevents attackers from recycling one deposit across identities, making a swarm costly in capital and forgone interest.
